model_reported.summary: Used the prior measurements to motivate a contrasting persistent-team experiment that removes repeated worksharing dispatch while retaining per-step synchronization.

model_reported.summary: No hardware or compiler details were supplied; this candidate uses the same standard OpenMP facilities already present in the source and does not assume target-specific features.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared only the supplied valid aggregate measurements, noted the close variant results and missing per-thread-budget breakdown, and left correctness and timing conclusions to the controller.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as context for another persistent-team implementation; these aggregate measurements do not establish which team lifetime is faster at each thread budget.
memory_lessons.claim: The per-step-team and persistent-worksharing candidates were both valid and measured about 0.241 seconds, much faster than the valid 0.464905-second baseline. Their mean-time difference is small relative to the ranges of their reported trials, and no separate one- and four-thread results are supplied.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a persistent team with fixed row ownership and explicit timestep barriers against the prior team variants at one and four threads.

proposal.hypothesis: The two valid prior OpenMP variants measured nearly the same aggregate time (0.241145 and 0.241645 seconds) against the 0.464905-second serial baseline, and the supplied outcomes do not separate one- from four-thread timings. This candidate tests a different cost: it keeps one team across all six timesteps but assigns contiguous row chunks once, replacing repeated worksharing dispatch with an explicit barrier after each step. Less dispatch overhead could help; the barriers or imbalance could offset it. Correctness and native timings, including initialization, remain for controller evaluation.

retained: Replace the serial six-step sweep with one persistent OpenMP team requesting no more than the positive threads budget and available row count.
Partition interior z/y rows deterministically into contiguous per-thread chunks instead of using repeated OpenMP worksharing loops.
Use an explicit barrier after each timestep so all output rows are complete before the next timestep reads them.
Preserve full buffer initialization, six-step even/odd buffer parity, stencil expression, and interior update bounds.
